memories.memory_text: I said hello, good evening, ma'am—real polite—like maybe someone would answer, but they just walked past like I wasn’t even there.
A boy came running and just—went right through me. I stumbled back like I got hit, but it wasn’t the body—it was like everything inside just froze.

I zipped in fast and dropped right into the middle of the kids—felt the rush as that first snowball hit Jamie square in the back of the head. His face went from annoyed to lit up like something clicked, and I knew it was working.

I kept the chaos going—snowballs flying, kids laughing, Pippa and Monty getting nailed outta nowhere. That moment when Pippa got hit and spun around yelling 'Jamie Bennett!'—I couldn't help but grin, knowing she had no idea it was me.
North poked me hard in the chest and demanded to know what my center was—like he could just dig it out of me with his finger.
He handed me that carved doll, all stern and armored, and when I opened it, there was a smaller, jollier version inside—like he was showing me some kind of secret self.
I remember crouching beside Tooth, asking why Pitch took the teeth, and then hearing her say they hold childhood memories—mine too. I couldn’t believe it: I had a life before I was Jack Frost.
I remember flying across the pond, feeling that surge—this was it, the key to who I was. When North said they’d help me get my memories back if I joined them, I didn’t hesitate. I said, 'I'm in.'
I hit it—froze that Nightmare right on the rooftop! Sandy, did you see that? I can't believe I actually nailed it!
He said it wasn't my fight—but when he stole those teeth, he made it personal. I remember raising my staff, knowing I had to stand with them.
I closed the window and told Baby Tooth we should get back.
Then I heard it — a voice laughing, calling my name... I don't know where it came from, but I swear I've heard it before.
I saw the box—my name was on it, 'Jack Frost'—and when I caught it, my hands froze the moment I realized what it was.
His voice kept coming from everywhere, whispering that I was afraid—afraid they'd never accept me—and I couldn't tell where he was, just shadows closing in.

I was holding Baby Tooth, trying to keep her warm, when I heard it—someone whispering my name, like a voice from nowhere. Then I felt this strange warmth in my pocket, and when I looked, the Tooth Box was glowing gold, pulsing like it was alive.

When the light got brighter, I saw flashes—kids laughing, a fire, my sister yelling at me to get down from a tree—then suddenly I was back there, young again, staring out at the snow in colonial clothes, my eyes brown, not blue. It was me, but a me I didn’t remember.
I held her gaze and told her not to look down, just to trust me—then made her laugh by pretending to wobble during our game of hopscotch on the ice.

I pulled her to safety with my staff, but the ice gave way beneath me—I fell in, couldn't claw my way out, and then... the Moon was there, shining down as everything went bright and cold and then... I opened my eyes, changed.
I saved her—I was the one who pulled my sister to safety. That’s why the Man in the Moon chose me.
I am a Guardian—I said it out loud, and then my staff sparked back to life when I forced the pieces together with everything I had.

I opened cage after cage, telling the Mini Teeth to go, but they just stood there—no spark, no movement. When Baby Tooth looked toward the Globe, I saw the lights flickering out… and I knew something was really wrong.
I landed and saw the globe—so dark, so empty—and I whispered, 'They're all going out...' like I could barely believe it.
I jumped up onto the globe and saw that one last flickering light—Jamie's. It was him. The only one left who still believed.
He said my name—Jamie said 'Jack Frost'—and I couldn't believe it. After 300 years, someone finally spoke it out loud.
I asked if he could hear me, if he could see me—and he nodded. Then I knew: he really sees me. The room exploded with snow when I jumped for joy.
I saw Jamie look right at me, called me by name—his eyes lit up like he finally remembered. I put my hand on his shoulder, and he smiled up at me like I belonged there.
Bunny froze when Jamie said I made him believe—his ears twitched, his voice cracked. For a second, I think he actually saw me, not just the snow or the trouble.
I fell hard from the sky, slammed into that dumpster, and crumpled to the ground—everything hurt, and I could barely get the words out: 'He's stronger. I can't beat him.'
Jamie's voice cracked as he said 'I'm scared,' and it hit me like a flash—suddenly I wasn't in the alley anymore, I was back on the ice with my sister saying the exact same thing.
I looked at Jamie and said we were gonna have a little fun instead—then it hit me, clear as ice: that's it, fun isn't just what I do, it's who I am.
I nailed Pitch with a snowball right in the face, then spotted a crate, a trash can lid, and a wok in the trash—knew we could use them to escape, and told Jamie we were going to get his friends.
I zipped through the quiet streets with Jamie, wind at my back, leaving a trail of ice behind us—then laughed as the Guardians tumbled after us on makeshift sleds, scared but grinning like kids.
I was gliding through the air, minding my own business, when suddenly Pippa turned her head and looked right at me—really saw me—for the first time, like she finally knew I was real.
I was about to step in front of Jamie to shield him, but then I felt this jolt—suddenly he was standing in front of *me*, small hand out, saying 'I will.' I froze. He was protecting *me*.

The black wave hit them and I braced for impact—but instead of fear, there was gold. Pure golden light bursting from their hands, turning the nightmare sand into dreamsand. I couldn't believe my eyes.
I landed hard on the roof—made sure Pitch heard me—then blasted a streak of frost straight at his Nightmares, watching them shatter under the ice.
I caught the little wooden doll North tossed me and opened my palm to see it—carved just like me, one of his Russian nesting dolls—and I couldn't help but smile, feeling like I finally belonged.
I saw Pitch freeze in terror when the Nightmares turned on him. I told him, 'Looks like it's your fear they smell.'

I looked up at the Moon and thought I saw a face—just for a second—and then Tooth came flying in, hugging me so tight I left the ground. I could feel her shaking with joy, and then Baby Tooth buzzed in, making her jump back all flustered.
North opened the book and asked if I was ready to make it official. A stern elf hit a horn nearby. North asked me to vow to guard the children’s hopes, wishes, and dreams. I paused before answering.

My name is Jack Frost -- how do I know that? The moon told me so. But that was all he ever told me. And that was a long, long time ago.
Look, this is all very flattering, but ah...you don't want me. You're all hard work and deadlines, and I'm snowballs and fun times. I'm not a Guardian.

But why, why wouldn't he tell me that himself? After 300 years this is his answer? To spend eternity like you guys cooped up in some, some hideout thinking of, of new ways to bribe kids? No no, that's not for me. No offense.

relations.relation_summary: Jack and Pitch are locked in a deeply antagonistic relationship defined by mutual hostility, direct confrontations, and opposing roles in the narrative. Social relationship evidence consistently frames them as enemies, with Pitch acting as the primary antagonist who attacks, threatens, and psychologically manipulates Jack. Key actions such as Pitch stealing Jack's memories, breaking his staff, and assaulting him with Nightmare sand establish a pattern of physical and emotional aggression. Jack repeatedly resists and counterattacks, using ice and frost to defend himself and confront Pitch, demonstrating active opposition. Their adversarial dynamic is further emphasized by Pitch's taunts about Jack's fear of non-belief and isolation—vulnerabilities he exploits to undermine Jack's confidence as a Guardian. Despite this enmity, a pivotal moment of temporary emotional resonance occurs when Jack listens to Pitch's monologue about longing for belief and family. In that moment, there is a brief connection rooted in shared experiences of loneliness and rejection, suggesting a complex layer beneath their conflict. However, this does not alter the fundamental opposition between them. Common events such as their confrontations in the cavern, the shadow pursuit in the corridor, and the violent clash where Pitch slams Jack into an iceberg wall reinforce the intensity and physicality of their conflict. North's arrival interrupts one such confrontation, underscoring how external forces shape their interactions. Ultimately, the relationship remains adversarial throughout, with no evidence of reconciliation or alliance. The brief moment of understanding does not evolve into cooperation but instead highlights the tragedy of their opposing paths. The relationship profoundly impacts Jack’s development, forcing him to confront his insecurities and ultimately reaffirm his role as a Guardian in direct defiance of Pitch’s worldview.

The relationship between Jack and North is multifaceted, rooted in mutual respect, emotional support, and a shared mission as Guardians. Social relationship evidence reveals a dynamic where North assumes a mentor and paternal role, consistently encouraging Jack, praising his efforts, and expressing concern for his safety—such as warning him to be careful and comforting him after Sandy's death. These interactions reflect deep care and a protective instinct, reinforced by physical affection like hugging and kissing Jack on the cheeks, which signifies warmth and familial-like attachment. North repeatedly invites Jack to join the Guardians, persists in seeking him out after battles, and acknowledges him as a vital ally, indicating trust and reliance on Jack’s participation. Jack, in turn, responds positively—smiling at North’s overtures, aligning himself with North during confrontations, and expressing shared purpose with the statement 'Same as you.' Their emotional dynamic evolves from initial resistance to full cooperative alignment, as seen when Jack joins North on the sleigh and they jointly respond to the crisis of the failing globe. Key events such as approaching the globe together, revealing tooth bags to Tooth, and North physically guiding Jack underscore their growing unity. The combination of supportive dialogue, physical gestures of affection, and repeated collaboration in urgent missions demonstrates that their relationship transforms from tentative inclusion into a strong, emotionally invested partnership grounded in duty, trust, and familial warmth.

Jack and Tooth share a multifaceted relationship defined by cooperation, mutual respect, and emotional support, evolving from initial tension to a strong bond of friendship and teamwork. Early in their interactions, hostility emerges when Tooth feels betrayed by Jack's indirect role in the disappearance of Baby Tooth and the tooth box, indicating a moment of conflict rooted in duty and trust. However, this tension is quickly overcome as both characters engage in numerous collaborative efforts, particularly in their shared mission as Guardians. Tooth actively helps Jack recover his lost memories by revealing that teeth preserve childhood recollections, guiding him to a mural and personally disclosing that his own memories are stored within the collection—acts that establish trust and deepen their connection. Jack reciprocates by expressing gratitude when Tooth defends him from BunnyMund’s criticism and when she deflects an attack by Pitch, showing mutual appreciation and loyalty. Their partnership is further solidified through joint events such as collecting teeth, where they work alongside other Guardians, and Tooth visibly acknowledges Jack’s contributions with warmth and gratitude. Physical acts of care—Tooth rescuing Jack after he collapses and Jack checking on her after her collision with a billboard—highlight their concern for each other’s well-being. Emotional support is also evident: Tooth offers Jack reassuring smiles during vulnerable moments, and Jack crouches beside her in solidarity when she is distressed, demonstrating empathy and unity. The relationship culminates in clear expressions of friendship, including a warm greeting after a rescue and a heartfelt hug, confirming their bond as both teammates and friends. Overall, the relationship evolves from suspicion to deep camaraderie, significantly influencing their behavior by fostering trust, encouraging mutual protection, and strengthening their commitment to the Guardians’ mission.

memories.memory_text: I remember the fiery gypsy violin music as the clouds parted, revealing my fortress in the massive ice canyon — hidden, incredible, and mine.
I chiseled the final details into the ice locomotive, my eye magnified through the jeweler's tool, and chuckled as it launched into the air with wings and jets.

I was about to scold the yeti for wrecking my train when he shouted about the Globe—I froze, then grabbed my sword and ran, heart pounding, because the Globe never alarms unless something is terribly wrong.

I saw the Globe of Belief—my lights, the children’s belief—snuffed out in waves, then swallowed by a crawling black sand that came from nowhere, and when it vanished, a shadow flashed across my walls with laughter echoing behind it.
I stood atop my fortress and unleashed the Northern Light—after so many years, the Guardians' Call surged into the sky, and I knew they would come.
I saw the Aurora flare across the sky and knew it was time — my voice rang out, calling every Guardian to action because the children were in danger.
I sounded the emergency signal, knowing the others would hear it — we have no time to waste if the enemy has returned.
I pointed to the globe and told the others—Pitch was here, black sand all over it, and then a shadow. I saw it, I felt it in my belly, something bad is coming.
After Bunny doubted me, I stood my ground—I know Pitch is up to something terrible, and I called them all here for a reason. I just need to know what to do next.
I spread my arms wide and greeted him with excitement—'Hey, there he is! Jack Frost!'—because this moment mattered, and I wanted him to feel it, even if he didn’t understand yet.
When he complained about the sack, I laughed and claimed it proudly—'Oh, good! That was my idea!'—because he needed to see I wasn’t intimidated by his resistance.
I told Jack to keep up as we moved through the factory—he was lagging, distracted by the yetis and toys, but I had no time to waste. There was work to do, and he needed to see how things run.

I leaned in and whispered to Jack that the elves don't really make the toys—we just let them believe that—then saw him glance over at the elves messing with ornaments and lights. It was a small truth, but one worth sharing.
I showed Jack the magic in my workshop—the toys coming alive, the lights, the flying planes—so he could feel the wonder I carry and protect as my center.

I grabbed the reins and wrapped them tight around my arms, then called out — 'Good! Let's go! Clear!' — and cracked the reins hard. The sleigh surged forward, and I felt the power beneath us, ready to fly.

As we hit the corkscrew, I glanced back and shouted, 'I hope you like the loopty loops!' — Bunny looked green, but I couldn't help it; the thrill of the ride and his fear made it too perfect not to say.

I held up the snow globe and said, 'I say, Tooth Palace,' and when the image appeared inside, I threw it forward and tore open a swirling portal through the sky—then shouted 'Hyah!' as I drove the sleigh into the vortex.
I was pulling the sleigh out of hyperdrive when these dark streaks came screaming toward us—something was terribly wrong.
I yanked the reins hard to the side, swerving through those black creatures as they tore past—had to keep everyone in the sleigh from getting hit.

I saw that foul Nightmare skulking ahead and didn’t hesitate — I thrust the reins into Jack’s hands and drew my sword. With one clean strike, I split it in two, and those stolen tooth boxes spilled out like broken promises.

The sleigh was barreling toward a pillar — I barely had time to shout, 'Jack, look out!' — then we crashed hard onto a platform. My heart pounded as I called up to Tooth, needing to know she was still with us.
I said 'He's gone' when we landed. Then I said Pitch would pay.
I saw Tooth weakening, the mural crumbling—then it hit me: 'Wait, wait, wait... Idea!! HAHH!! We will collect the teeth!'—and I shouted it like a war cry, feeling the plan ignite in my chest.
I BOOMED up through the chimneys, laughing and shouting — 'A race? Is it a race??' — feeling the rush of rooftops beneath my boots and the night air crackling with energy.
Mid-leap between rooftops, I burst out of a chimney with a bang and shouted 'EPIC!!' — the word exploding into the night just like me.
We are flying over a Middle Eastern city at night in my sleigh, the full moon above us.
I was right there at the boy's bedside, about to grab the tooth—easy job—when Sandy just floated in and took it right from under me. That's my tooth! Sandy! Sandy!
I stood there with my bag of teeth, feeling proud—until Tooth asked if we’d actually been leaving gifts, and I realized none of us had. My chest tightened when the others looked down, ashamed.
I climb through the window with my sack of teeth, call out to the group, and ask Tooth how she's feeling. She says she feels believed in, and I laugh.
I placed my hand on Jack's shoulder and told him Sandy would be proud—he needed to know he belonged, even if he couldn't remember his past.

I remember the floor shaking first, then that cursed black sand tearing through the factory, wrapping around the globe, and then *he* appeared—Pitch, laughing, declaring Christmas over. My toys were falling, my Yetis terrified, and I could feel it—the attack wasn’t just on the workshop, but on the children.
I called out to my children as I climbed from the wreckage, but when I stood, my back gave out—I couldn't hold myself up anymore. That's when I knew it was true: my powers were gone.
Jamie said, 'It is you! I knew it wasn't a dream.' He saw me. Jack was there too.

memories.memory_text: I reached into that sweet, glowing dream and touched the unicorn—just one finger—and watched it turn black and crumble. The way the girl flinched in her sleep... delicious.
I shaped the black sand into a snarling Nightmare and sent it flying out the window to join the others—my army rising. The wait really is over.

I stepped out of the alley into the street, keeping clear of the moonlight, and looked up at the Moon—my old 'friend'—before declaring my Nightmares ready and throwing the challenge straight back at him.

I remember the screams rising from the campfire as my shadow climbed the mountain—how they trembled, how small they looked. Those were the days when fear fed me, and I stood beneath the moon, smiling at what I had become.
I leaned in close to the Guardians and told them it was all about to change — their precious belief, their power, everything they stood for. The look on their faces was priceless.
I heard the crack behind me, turned, and saw the column crumbling — then told them, 'Oh look, it's happening already.' I could feel the belief slipping away, just as I planned.
I felt the Nightmare dissolve under my glare, its sand twisting into Sandman’s shape between my fingers before I crushed it—those lights still burning on the globe, mocking me.
I cowered on the ground, looking up at Sandy and Jack, my voice trembling—'Okay, easy! You can't blame me for trying, Sandy.' I let them think they'd won, that I was weak, afraid.
I stood up mid-sentence, cutting through the act—'You can have `em back!'—and as the Nightmares erupted from the storm drains and rooftops, I grabbed Onyx's mane and leaned in, grinning. 'Boo!'
I pulled myself out of the mud, cold and soaked, but I could feel it—the fear returning, and it made me smile.
I saw the bright glow of the portal close after the sleigh vanished, and my Nightmares swarmed back to me—finally, fear was spreading again.
I saw the drawers full of baby teeth, and for a moment, all I could think about was finding my own name—just one box with 'Jack' on it would tell me who I really was.
I spoke from the shadows, telling Jack he was afraid of something, and I could see it in him.
I stepped out of the shadows behind Jack and said, 'Happy Easter, Jack,' watching his face fall as he saw the shattered eggs all around him.
I stepped forward and told Jack I understood his loneliness — being cast out, not believed in, longing for a family — and offered him a way out of the isolation we both knew too well.
When Jack refused, I didn't hesitate — I summoned my Nightmare sand, closed in, and crushed his staff beneath my foot, leaving him broken and helpless on the ice.
I rose from the black sand swirling around the globe, cackling as the Yetis and Elves scattered in terror—I could feel their fear rising like smoke.
I announced they were all free to go—no more toys this year, not ever again—and the look of defeat on that Yeti’s face made it perfect.
I stood before my globe and watched the last flickers of light vanish — they were all going out, just as I planned.
I was counting them down—one by one, snapping with glee as each light died—only one stubborn flicker left, and no matter how I snapped, it refused to go out.

I felt the cold rush of Jack's ice blast hit my sand, but it was useless—he looked shocked when I absorbed it like it was nothing. Then I charged forward and unleashed a storm of Nightmares that sent him crashing down, helpless.

I rode in on Onyx, watching them huddle around the boy like broken shields—weak, afraid, and utterly defeated. The fear in the air was thick, and I couldn't help but smile as I told them how happy I was to see them suffer.
A snowball exploded in my face—right as I was making my move—cold, sudden, undignified, and then the boy snickered, actually snickered, as if I were some joke.
I stood atop the building, smiling as my wave of Nightmare sand surged through the town—finally, they would all feel the fear I commanded.
I watched in disbelief as the black sand hit the children and burst into golden Dreamsand—they believed, and my Nightmares unraveled before my eyes.
I was savoring the chaos in the streets, smiling as my Nightmares did their work, when a sudden THUD made me turn—Jack was there on the roof, already sending a streak of frost at my creations.
I was about to strike Jack when Tooth burst in, knocking my arrow aside—then Bunny came roaring out of a chimney, and in an instant, my Nightmares disintegrated around me.
I slipped into the shadow to get away, but North was already leaping off the roof, scimitars in hand, cutting through the air right at me.
I rose from the ground, shaping my scythe from black sand, ready to strike—but then they were all around me, knocking me down again and again.
I was just about to strike Jack down when a golden whip coiled around my hands—Sandy’s whip—and yanked me back, stopping me cold.
I was trying to escape, but then I slipped on the ice and looked up to see North grinning down at me—then Tooth threw a quarter in my face and punched me, knocking out a tooth.
